prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Denver. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Denver for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — first I need one quick detail: do you mean Denver proper or the Denver metro area, and do you have a zip code or neighborhood? Also tell me whether you have a dental plan (insurance) or any preferences (oral surgeon vs periodontist, same‑day teeth/All‑on‑4, sedation options, budget). With that I’ll give a short, prioritized list of specific practices to call.

Meanwhile, here’s immediate, actionable guidance so you can start calling today.

Which types of practices to call (and why)
- Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeons (OMS): best for complex extractions, bone grafting, sinus lifts, sedation/general anesthesia, and implant placement in difficult cases. Call them if you anticipate surgery or want full surgical care.
- Periodontists: specialists in the gums and supporting structures; excellent for implants when you need bone augmentation or soft‑tissue (esthetic) work.
- Prosthodontists: specialists in replacing teeth (crowns, bridges, implant prostheses). Call them when you want the best functional/esthetic restoration on top of the implant.
- Multidisciplinary implant centers / dental offices with in‑house surgeons and prosthodontists: convenient “one‑stop” care; often coordinate surgery and final restoration.
- Dental practices offering digital implant workflows (CBCT, guided surgery, intraoral scanning) or same‑day provisional teeth (All‑on‑4) — call if you want faster, more predictable treatment.

What to ask when you call (use this checklist)
- Do you place dental implants in‑office, and which specialist (OMS, periodontist, prosthodontist) will perform the surgery and who will restore the crown?  
- How many implants does the doctor place per year and how long have they been placing implants? (volume and experience matter.)  
- Do you use cone‑beam CT (CBCT) and guided implant placement? Will I get a treatment plan and cost estimate in writing?  
- What implant systems/brands do you use (e.g., Nobel Biocare, Straumann, Zimmer, Dentsply/Implantium)? (Reputable brands and warranties are good.)  
- Will I need bone grafting or sinus lift? If so, how is that handled and what are the additional costs?  
- What are the full costs (surgery, grafting, abutment, final crown/prosthesis, follow‑ups)? Do you offer financing or payment plans?  
- Are sedation/general anesthesia options available? What are credentials/monitoring?  
- Do you provide a written estimate and a timeline from surgery to final crown?  
- What warranty or follow‑up care is included for the implant and the crown?  
- Can I see before/after photos and patient references or reviews?  

Red flags to avoid
- Vague answers about who will restore the crown or who will handle complications.  
- No use of CBCT for treatment planning on single/multiple implants.  
- Unclear total pricing or significantly lower cost without explanation (may indicate shortcuts).  
- No written treatment plan or timeline.

How I can help next
- If you give me your Denver neighborhood or zip code plus whether you have insurance or a preference for a surgical specialist vs a multidisciplinary center, I’ll produce a prioritized list of 6–8 specific practices to call in your area, each with a short reason (e.g., OMS with sedation, prosthodontist known for esthetic restorations, implant center offering same‑day teeth, insurance-friendly offices).
